newsitem.title: UK: Consumer optimism in Britain slows -- study.
newsitem.headline: Consumer optimism in Britain slows -- study.

text.p: Consumer spending in Britain is likely to rise 4.5 percent this year, the fastest rate since the recession at the beginning of the 1990s but growth in consumer confidence has slowed, economic consultancy Business Strategies Ltd said.
"Growth in consumer confidence has slowed down across the country," it said in its January consumer Market Quarterly Bulletin.

Business Strategies director David Fell said: "These results could be interpreted as the first tentative indication that the feelgood factor is starting to fade slightly in some places. Against that, it has to be acknowledged that most people across the country still have a pretty robust view of economic prospects."
Fell said optimism about household finances for the coming 12 months was improving at a slower rate.

"Financial worries are often a reflection of fears over job security, yet paradoxically, these are receding still further," he added. "But concerns about inflation are starting to increase, having fallen through most of the 1990s."
Worries about inflation might reflect fears about the prospect of higher interest rates, he added.
